facts.statement: The genus Angolasaurus was first named by Miguel Telles Antunes in 1964.
facts.quote: authority: Antunes, 1964

facts.statement: In 1994, the species was synonymized with Platecarpus bocagei by Lingham-Soliar.
facts.quote: synonyms: Platecarpus bocagei Lingham-Soliar, 1994

facts.statement: Angolasaurus is an extinct genus of mosasaur known as the "Angola lizard".
facts.quote: Angolasaurus ("Angola lizard") is an extinct genus of mosasaur.

facts.statement: Angolasaurus is one of the few Turonian mosasaurs known to have a transatlantic distribution.
facts.quote: Its wide geographic range make it one of the only Turonian mosasaurs with a transatlantic range.

facts.statement: Antunes originally described Angolasaurus based on a partial skull and skeleton found in 1964.
facts.quote: First named in 1964 by Miguel Telles Antunes on the basis of a partial skull and skeleton

facts.statement: Fieldwork conducted between 2005 and 2009 uncovered at least two new skeletons of Angolasaurus.
facts.quote: Fieldwork between 2005 and 2009 recovered at least two new Angolasaurus skeletons.

facts.statement: CT scans of the type skull and a new skull revealed detailed interior braincase structures.
facts.quote: One new skull as well as the type skull were CT scanned to reveal intricate details of the interior braincase

facts.statement: Two individuals from the Eagle Ford Formation of Texas were assigned to Angolasaurus in 2007.
facts.quote: In 2007, two individuals from the Eagle Ford Formation of Texas were described as belonging to the genus Angolasaurus

facts.statement: Fossils of Angolasaurus date from the Turonian to the Coniacian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Turonian-Coniacian

facts.statement: Remains of Angolasaurus have been found in Angola, the United States, Brazil, and Niger.
facts.quote: Definite remains from this genus have been recovered from the Turonian and Coniacian of Angola, and possibly the Coniacian of the United States, the Turonian of Brazil, and the Maastrichtian of Niger.

facts.statement: The species Angolasaurus bocagei is known exclusively from the Itombe Formation.
facts.quote: Angolasaurus bocagei, recovered only from the Itombe Formation

facts.statement: Angolasaurus fossils from the Dukamaje Formation consist of vertebrae from individuals of different growth stages.
facts.quote: Known from the Dukamaje Formation on the basis of a few vertebrae of varying ontogenetic stages

facts.statement: Angolasaurus fossils have been recovered from the Eagle Ford Formation in Texas.
facts.quote: Angolasaurus is known from the Eagle Ford Formation of Texas.

facts.statement: The skull of Angolasaurus contained 11 maxillary, 4 premaxillary, and 12 dentary teeth.
facts.quote: Its skull housed 11 maxillary teeth, 4 premaxillary teeth, and 12 dentary teeth.

facts.statement: Angolasaurus possessed a tail fluke, forward-lying nostrils, and keeled scales to aid in swimming.
facts.quote: The phylogenetic relationship of Angolasaurus indicates that individuals of this genus possessed a tail fluke, more forward-lying nostrils, and keeled scales for hydrodynamic efficiency.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Angolasaurus had dark dorsal patterning to help with thermoregulation due to cooling sea temperatures.
facts.quote: Due to declining sea temperatures in the area that Angolasaurus inhabited, as well as the later Bientiaba locality, it has been hypothesized that it and the other mosasaurs inhabiting its region may have had an increased coverage of dark patterning on its dorsal surface to aid in thermoregulation.

facts.statement: Recent analyses place Angolasaurus in a basal position within the subfamily Plioplatecarpinae.
facts.quote: While at one point considered a species of Platecarpus, recent phylogenetic analyses have placed it between the (then) plioplatecarpines Ectenosaurus and Selmasaurus, maintaining a basal position within the plioplatecarpinae.

facts.statement: Angolasaurus is considered basal to the clade containing Tylosaurinae and Plioplatecarpinae but belongs to neither subfamily.
facts.quote: The most recent major phylogenetic analysis conducted on the mosasauridae placed Angolasaurus as basal to the clade composed of the russellosaurine subfamilies Tylosaurinae and Plioplatecarpinae, and part of neither.

facts.statement: The parent group of Angolasaurus is Russellosaurina.
facts.quote: Parent group: Russellosaurina

facts.statement: Angolasaurus belongs to the family Mosasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Mosasauridae

facts.statement: Angolasaurus is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: It is debated whether Angolasaurus fossils from the United States, Brazil, and Niger definitively belong to this genus.
facts.quote: possibly the Coniacian of the United States, the Turonian of Brazil, and the Maastrichtian of Niger.

rejected.statement: Two teeth previously attributed to Platecarpus were reassigned to Angolasaurus in a 2007 study.
rejected.quote: The same abstract assigned two teeth previously assigned to Platecarpus to Angolasaurus.

rejected.statement: Angolasaurus was a small mosasaur with a skull length of 40 cm and an estimated total length of 4 meters.
rejected.quote: Angolasaurus was a small mosasaur, with a skull length estimated at 40 cm, suggesting a possible total length of about 4 meters (13 feet)
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'was a small mosasaur with a skull length'
